lead: Weapons and armour a private person may own, from swords, knives and historical armour to firearms, air guns and archery, organised by weapon family, then kind, then named archetype; legal classes are kept off the tree.

depts.note: Antique, modern-made and replica blades together; period and origin are versions, not kinds.

b.v: stainless wall-hanger · mono-steel through-hardened · differentially hardened · folded/laminated traditional
b.w: Collector and practitioner guides separate decorative from functional blades by steel and heat treatment.

b.v: rat-tail · full tang peened or pinned (mekugi)
b.w: Tang construction decides whether a sword is safe to cut with.

b.v: replica · modern traditional (shinsakutō) · antique with papers (NBTHK) / provenance
b.w: Nihontō papers and auction provenance set value for antiques.

s.brief: Organise by Oakeshott typology (types X–XXII) for medieval swords, Petersen types for Viking swords; archetypes = named historical originals and typology types (e.g. Oakeshott XIIIa, XVIIIa), then makers' reproductions as versions (Albion, Arms & Armor, Regenyei, Kingston Arms, Windlass, Cold Steel, Darksword). Add Viking sword, basket-hilted broadsword, and estoc. Sabre: national patterns (1796 Light Cavalry, Hungarian). Trim SKU lists of cheap replicas to versions under archetypes.

k.brief: bastard / hand-and-a-half as aliases; Oakeshott XV–XX archetypes
messer and grosse messer as archetypes
Scottish basket hilt (claymore), schiavona, mortuary sword

s.brief: Build a nihontō register: period (kotō, shintō, shinshintō, gendaitō, shinsakutō) → school (Gokaden: Yamashiro, Yamato, Bizen, Sōshū, Mino) → smith (Masamune, Muramasa, Kotetsu, Kiyomaro…). Versions: antique / shinsakutō / iaitō / replica. Add traditions entries for the five Gokaden schools. Cut modern-replica SKU lists (Hanbon, BattleBlades) to a few versions.

k.brief: unsharpened alloy or steel practice sword for iaidō

s.n: Swords of Asia, Africa & the Middle East
s.brief: Non-European swords: archetypes by region and named patterns (e.g. Chinese jian, liuyedao, dadao; Persian shamshir; Indian talwar, khanda; Ottoman kilij, yataghan; Philippine kampilan; Burmese dha; Tuareg takoba; Ethiopian shotel). Add traditions entries (e.g. wootz / Damascus steel, Chinese Longquan swordsmithing).
Koshirae collecting: tsuba schools (Kinai, Higo, Shōami, Gotō, Nara) as archetypes; menuki and fuchi-kashira by school; European scabbards as types. Add habaki.

depts.note: Fighting and hunting knives only; EDC and utility knives are in Tools, kitchen knives in Kitchen.

b.w: Knife reviews compare edge retention and corrosion by steel.

b.v: fixed full tang · folding lock type
b.w: Strength and safety follow construction.

s.brief: Archetypes: Buck 110/119, Randall Model 1, Ka-Bar USMC, Fairbairn-Sykes, Bowie originals, Mk 3 trench knife; historic daggers (rondel, baselard, bollock, stiletto, kris). Bayonets by pattern (M1, Mauser 98k, SA 1907…). Add kukri, seax, trench knife, kris.

k.brief: keris; UNESCO ICH Indonesian kris tradition entry

s.brief: Butterfly knife: balisong archetypes (Benchmade 42, Bear & Son); automatic: OTF vs side-opening as types; throwing knives and shuriken (hira-shuriken, bō-shuriken types).

depts.note: Sporting, collector and antique guns; legal classes are not used as categories.

b.w: The hunting-rifle guide starts from the shooter.

b.w: Calibre and action follow the use.

Trim the 27 powders to the market-covering makers (Hodgdon, Alliant, Vihtavuori, Accurate/Ramshot, Winchester). Add reloading press (single-stage, turret, progressive; Dillon, RCBS, Lee, Hornady) and die set.

b.w: Scope tests compare glass and turret repeatability.

s.brief: Archetypes: Trijicon ACOG, Aimpoint CompM, EOTech holographic, Leupold VX line, Zeiss/Swarovski hunting scopes, LPVO as type. Add night-vision / thermal weapon sight.
Restraint: keep platform-level kinds; trim magazine list to market makers (Magpul, OEM).
Holster carry styles as types (IWB, OWB, paddle, shoulder). Add gun case and gun cleaning kit. Gun safes stay in Home Safety & Security.

depts.note: Traditional bows are variety; target and hunting gear tier. Archery accessories handed over from Bags & Accessories land here.

b.w: Fit to the archer before anything else.
World Archery and field-archery classes.

s.brief: Traditional bows from traditions: English longbow (Mary Rose), Japanese yumi (kyūdō), Mongol, Turkish, Korean gakgung and Hungarian horse bows, American flatbow (Bear, Howard Hill). Compound archetypes (Hoyt, Mathews, Bowtech, PSE); Olympic recurve ILF as type. Traditions entries for yumi-making and composite horse bows.

k.brief: composite / Asiatic bow; Mongol, Turkish, Korean, Hungarian archetypes

s.brief: Arrow shaft materials as types (wood, aluminium, carbon); arrowheads: broadhead/field point/bodkin. Add bow sight, release aid and stabiliser.
Slingshot archetypes (Wham-O, Barnett, Daisy); add the shepherd's sling (Balearic, Andean).
European and Asian polearms with named archetypes (Swiss halberd, Lucerne hammer, yari, guandao, ji). Add bill, partisan, bardiche, guandao.
Archetypes: Dane axe, bearded axe, Hudson Bay tomahawk, pipe tomahawk, flanged mace, morning star, horseman's pick, kanabō.
Okinawan kobudō, Chinese wushu and Filipino arnis apparatus. Merge bō and Chinese gùn into one staff kind with types. Add escrima sticks and jō.

b.w: Defence-product tests compare range and failure rates.
